verdict_summary: Both round-1 load-bearing discrepancies (A: false negative on CDE 2026 MLK; B: untested 'web.archive.org unreachable' claim and the superseded ICE 2026 product-group headers) are fully resolved, and all four advisories are either answered or still correctly disclosed. Independently: 53 of 53 indexed artifacts re-hash; ten cited documents re-fetched live and byte-compared, ten identical (including the new CDE 26-01 PDF and the new ICE 20260609 calendar); the Wayback capture 20260728113521 replays byte-identical to live; a fresh CDX enumeration reproduces the saved ifus_notices_cdx_2025-2027.json byte-for-byte and re-confirms that no 2026 ICE MLK or Presidents Day notice is archived; 121 ICE-calendar family entries were machine-checked cell-by-cell against the PDFs with zero mismatches, and a further ~60 entries across CFE/Eurex/ICE-notice/CDE were re-read by hand with every status, instant and zone matching the operator's print; no instant is inferred from another year; every one of the 203 family entries is now T1 and none is 'unknown'. No load-bearing defect remains. Four non-blocking advisories are recorded below.

HAND-CHECKED: CFE — all 12 CSV rows reproduce character-for-character, including the 'None' cells, the two-segment ETH strings and the day-of-week parentheticals; every close_instant is the instant printed in its own row with the correct Central offset (10:30 -06:00 on 01-19, 02-16, 11-26; 08:30 -05:00 on 04-03; 10:30 -05:00 on 05-25, 06-19, 07-03, 09-07; 08:30/12:15 -06:00 on 11-27 and 12-24). ICE per-holiday notices — Good Friday (softs+Canola Closed/None; MSCI/FANG+/NYSE/FTSE 'Late Open - 5:00 am / Early Close – 9:15 am, No TAS trading'; USDX group 'Late Open - 5:00 am / Early Close - 11:15 am, No TAS Trading' — the inconsistent en-dash/hyphen and the capital T are reproduced as printed; Gold/Silver and Financial NG Closed; Apr 6 'Sugar No. 11, Coffee “C” and Cocoa - late open at 7:30 am'), Memorial Day (2:30 / 1:00 / 1:00 / Closed / 'Early Close 1:30 pm' with no dash), Juneteenth (2:30 / 1:00 / 1:00 / Gold 'Early Close - 1:30 pm' with Regular settlement times / 1:30), Independence Day revised (same set, plus Jul 6 'Late Open for Cotton: 8:00 am'), Labor Day (1:00 / 1:00 / USDX 'Regular Hours, TAS trading will not be held' correctly classed normal under LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY / 1:30 / Gold 1:30), Columbus Day (Canola closed, all others regular) — every instant carried at -04:00 (NY EDT), zone recorded as the operator prints it ('all times shown in NY time'). CDE — 25-42, 26-01, 26-05, 26-12, 26-23, 26-27.1, 26-29, 26-36: every OPEN/START and CLOSE/ROLL cell matches the grid, including the operator's own inconsistent zero-padding ('9/07 19:00 CT' in 26-36, '05/25 17:00 CT' in 26-23) and the column headers 'CLOSE/ROLL' vs 'ROLL'. Zone 'CT' as printed.

independent_checks.check: CME trading-hours service (T2) for any 2019+ holiday listed as missing
independent_checks.detail: Every venue in this task — CFE/Cboe Futures Exchange, Eurex, ICE Futures U.S., Coinbase Derivatives, SMFE/Kraken Derivatives Exchange — is outside CME Group. CME's trading-hours service publishes CME/CBOT/NYMEX/COMEX product windows only and cannot source a session for any identity in this file, so no missing[] entry here can be closed by it. Recorded explicitly rather than silently skipped.

203 family entries across 43 holiday dates; status distribution closed 90 / normal 47 / modified 36 / early_close 28 / late_open 2; ZERO entries with status 'unknown' and ZERO entries below T1 (round 0 had one 'unknown' at 'T1 (absence of document)'). Every day-of-week in the file agrees with the operator's printed weekday. LAW-UTC-DATES: every retrieval time in the -fix INDEX.md matches the file's own mtime converted to UTC (07:41-07:49 UTC against AEST mtimes 17:41-17:49), and 2026-09-12 is today's UTC date — no future-dated record. LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY is applied correctly: ICE's 2026 Juneteenth equity-index companion notice, which I re-read, contains only last-trade-day and final-settlement/SOQ content and keys nothing; 'TAS trading will not be held' is treated as a trade-type restriction, not a boundary. The Eurex 2027 rows are tiered 'T1 (operator-published but expressly INDICATIVE/PRELIMINARY — not an unconditional dated future under LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES)', which is the right handling.

advisories.detail: The corrected CFE rule enumerates only the rows whose Regular Trading Hours cell prints 'None'. It does not mention the two rows that print an actual RTH range — 'Thanksgiving Early Close,2026-11-27,08:30:00 - 12:15:00,…' and 'Christmas Early Close,2026-12-24,08:30:00 - 12:15:00,…' — which the JSON (correctly) records as early_close with open_instant 08:30 and close_instant 12:15 Central. The JSON is right; only the restated rule is incomplete. Suggested wording: '… a holiday row is an early close when it prints a Regular-Trading-Hours range that ends before the normal 15:00 CT close, OR when its Extended-Trading-Hours string ends at an instant on the holiday date; and closed when it prints no Regular Trading Hours and no session ends on the date (2026-01-01) or prints "None / None" (2026-12-25).'

The row presents the Contentful hyperlink node as a verbatim quotation with plain slashes and single-escaped quotes ('…"uri":"https://images.ctfassets.net/…/Market_Notice_26-01_MLK_Holiday.pdf"},"content":…') and says 'the hrefs are `/`-escaped'. The saved bytes actually read `\\"uri\\":\\"https:\\u002F\\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\\u002F…`, i.e. the slashes are \\u002F-escaped inside a doubly-escaped JSON string. The substance is correct and I resolved the URL from those bytes and re-fetched the PDF byte-identical, so nothing load-bearing turns on it — but a quotation offered as verbatim should be the bytes, with the normalisation stated. Corrected text: 'hrefs appear as `\\u002F`-escaped URLs inside a doubly-escaped embedded JSON payload; unescape `\\u002F` to `/` before use. Bytes as stored: `\\"uri\\":\\"https:\\u002F\\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\\u002Fk3n74unfin40\\u002FjJEoZRkAZ0JlPC3UcJ2CL\\u002Fd71ac89c5cd10783b9a7e11f449d1424\\u002FMarket_Notice_26-01_MLK_Holiday.pdf\\"`.'

The round-0 INDEX.md is correctly left byte-intact, but it still asserts, with no pointer to the correction, three statements the fix has shown to be false: the header claim 'web.archive.org was unreachable from this machine for the whole session' (line 9), the cde_notices row's '**No 2026 MLK notice is listed** (26-01/26-02/26-04 are absent from the table)' (line 48), and interpretive note 2's 'Only 2026-12-25 has "None / None" and is a full closure' (line 66). It contains the string 'fix' zero times. A reader who opens only that file is misled. Remedy that preserves the bytes: add a sibling file raw/cfe-eurex-ice-cde-smfe-2026-2027/SUPERSEDED.md containing one line — 'Lines 9, 48 and 66 of INDEX.md are superseded; see ../cfe-eurex-ice-cde-smfe-2026-2027-fix/INDEX.md § CORRECTIONS (round-1 fix, 2026-09-12 UTC).' — and index it in the -fix INDEX.md.
